subject: Vega-7B elevated errors and mitigation timeline
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novacorp.com>, support@novacorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vega-7B elevated errors and mitigation timeline

Hi Elena / NovaCorp team,

Quick update from infra: since ~08:50 UTC we’ve observed an elevated rate of 5xx and timeout responses for requests routed to our Vega-7B model (text-generation endpoints only). The error spike is concentrated on longer sequence generation (>1k tokens) and certain batched workloads.

What we’ve done so far:
- Throttled adaptive batching and disabled a recently shipped kernel optimization that appears correlated with increased KV cache pressure.
- Rolled fallback routing for new requests to Vega-7B-lite where compatible; existing long-running sessions may still surface errors while KV caches warm.
- Increased autoscaling headroom on the Vega pool to reduce queueing.

Immediate customer impact: you may see intermittent 502/504 responses and elevated latency for some calls. We recommend temporarily switching critical flows to Vega-7B-lite or using our alternative model tag (vega-7b-compat) which we’ve validated against your prompt sets.

We’re attaching a short log snippet for the window we investigated (vega-7b-log-snippet.txt). We’ll follow up with a stability summary and a timeline for a full post-incident review.

Requested from you: can you confirm whether NovaCorp saw production failures for downstream features (chat sessions, batch scoring) and share any representative request IDs? That will help us prioritize replay and log correlation.

Status page (live): https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/20270529-vega7b
Postmortem draft (internal link to be shared once we have a root cause): https://drive.google.com/fake-drive/vega7b-postmortem-draft

Sorry for the disruption — we’re treating this as high priority. I’ll post a recovery update within the next 4 hours or sooner if we have a mitigation that eliminates customer impact.

—
Jonas Weber
Sr Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-29T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Vega-7B incident — next actions and owner list

Team — summary + immediate asks:

Observed: elevated 5xx/timeout rate on Vega-7B for long sequences and some batched workloads (start ~08:50 UTC). External customer (NovaCorp) reporting 504s and specific request ids.

What we’ve done: throttled batching, disabled kernel opt, routing fallback to vega-7b-lite for new traffic.

Action items (owner):
- Marissa: validate fallback routing coverage across regions (us-east/us-west) and confirm which clients remain pinned to Vega-7B. Please provide a list of customers still on direct Vega routes by 10:15 PT.
- Ben: escalate teams to look at kernel optimization revert logs and verify that disabling it cleared the KV pressure metrics; share any traces that show increased memory churn.
- Soojin (Ops): collect a 10-minute contiguous trace window around 08:45–08:55 UTC and extract representative request ids (include Elena’s ids). Drop artifacts in the shared drive link.

Customer comms: I’ve told NovaCorp they can use vega-7b-lite; we should confirm the compatibility tests for their prompt shapes. If fallback is acceptable, prepare a quick runbook for support to switch customers.

Risk/next steps: if errors do not drop, we may need to roll a config revert to last known-good kernel set and run a controlled canary. Ben and Soojin — please update within 30 minutes with telemetry.

Thanks — Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@novacorp.com>, support@novacorp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-01T15:34:00-07:00
Subject: Vega-7B incident resolved — stabilization summary and next steps

Hi Elena — following up with a closure update and next steps. Thanks for the sample request ids; they helped narrow the window.

What we found and did:
- Root cause (summary): a kernel optimization we shipped to improve attention kernel throughput introduced edge-case KV cache thrashing under certain long-sequence + batch concurrency patterns. That thrashing caused transient memory pressure which surfaced as 502/504s for in-flight requests.
- Mitigation applied: we reverted the optimization in the Vega serving pool and enabled additional cache backpressure controls. We then rerouted traffic back from vega-7b-lite to Vega-7B in stages and monitored for 48 hours.
- Result: error rates returned to baseline within ~3 hours of the revert; we validated with NovaCorp test traffic and your reported request ids (req_us_east_4512/4513) show successful replays post-fix.

What we’re delivering:
- A full post-incident report with timelines, artifacts (traces, configuration diffs), and preventive actions by 2027-06-04 EOD. Draft will be shared to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/fake-drive/vega7b-postmortem-draft
- A set of recommended guardrails: staged kernel rollout gating, additional KV cache metrics exported to customers who opt-in, and a fallback routing default for long-sequence traffic.
- If you experienced measurable customer impact, we will evaluate usage credit per our incident response policy — please flag impacted invoices or estimate token loss and we’ll include that in the review.

Attachments: vega-7b-stability-notes-20270529.txt (contains timelines and short log excerpts).

Again, apologies for the disruption. If you’d like a short sync to walk through the postmortem draft and any client-facing language, I’m available tomorrow morning PT.
